# Vendored Third-Party Assets

Fetched by `tools/vendor.sh`. Do not hand-edit.

| Asset | Package | Version | License | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crepe.bundle.mjs` + `theme/` | `@milkdown/crepe` | 7.22.0 | MIT | https://github.com/Milkdown/milkdown |
| `codemirror.bundle.mjs` | `codemirror` | 6.0.2 | MIT | https://github.com/codemirror/basic-setup |
| `highlight.min.js` | `highlight.js` | 11.11.1 | BSD-3-Clause | https://github.com/highlightjs/highlight.js |
| `mermaid.min.js` | `mermaid` | 11.6.0 | MIT | https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid |

Milkdown bundles ProseMirror (MIT, https://prosemirror.net) and CodeMirror.
CodeMirror bundles @codemirror/* and @lezer/* packages (MIT,
https://github.com/codemirror).
Highlight.js provides the common browser language build used for markdown
source overlays and fenced code block highlighting.
Mermaid renders local fenced `mermaid` diagrams and assistant previews.

## Integrity

Every file in this directory has a SHA-256 recorded in
[`tools/vendor-digests.txt`](../../../tools/vendor-digests.txt), regenerated by
`tools/vendor.sh` and verified by `tools/verify-vendor.sh` on every CI run.

The digests matter more here than for an ordinary dependency. `tools/vendor.sh`
fetches these bundles over the network, and `crepe.bundle.mjs` is then patched
in place to remove an esm.sh Node-polyfill import that would 404 under the Wails
asset server. The committed bundle therefore matches **no** upstream artifact,
so re-downloading cannot tell you whether these bytes are the ones that were
reviewed. The recorded digest is the only durable record.

Verification never touches the network, so it checks what is committed rather
than what a fresh download happens to return today.
